findings.message: The new accept guard is a fix for the round-1 B4 major, but its test has only two rows: still open and released since. B2 asks for the named case plus at least two others. Missing rows: a proposal withdrawn after the suggestion was made (setOwnerIn refuses it, with a different message), and one that got a named owner since (the hasNoOwner branch). Also, the 'released' row sets the phase with a direct owner SQL update instead of the real move or release path, so the test never shows the guard firing on a state the service actually produces. Fix: add the withdrawn row and the named-since row. Reach the released state through the real service and leave the agent's tidy unrun, so the race the guard exists for is the thing the test drives.
findings.scenario: Delete the `needsOwner` line in proposal-kinds.ts → the released row fails, as it should. But change setOwnerIn's withdrawn refusal, or move the guard's order → the table still passes, because neither the withdrawn path nor the owned-since path has a row.

findings.message: The round-1 finding asked that the chip, the pin offer, the agent's Suggested owner and its accept guard all follow one rule. The offer and the accept guard now call `needsOwner`. The agent still decides whether to suggest an owner with its own copy of that rule: `open(p)` (line 25: not withdrawn and phase not released) combined with `hasNoOwner`. The two copies agree today, so there is no wrong behaviour yet. If `needsOwner` changes (for example, to also exclude verified proposals), the agent will keep making suggestions that the accept guard then refuses. Fix: have the agent call `needsOwner({ ownerUserId, ownerName, phase, withdrawn: isWithdrawn(p) })` when it decides whether to suggest, and in tidy() when it decides which suggestions to take back.

When `proposalNow` finds no row (the key doesn't exist, or the viewer can't see it), `was` falls back to "Unassigned". The card then shows a missing proposal as an open one that needs an owner, instead of saying it wasn't found. Fix: show "–" (the card's existing placeholder for a missing title) or say the proposal wasn't found.
